item.description:
“C vs C++ Pointer to Pointer vs Array of Arrays Memory Allocation Explained”

Understanding Pointer to Pointer vs. Array of Arrays Memory Allocation

The core of this issue lies in how these data types are laid out in memory and consequently accessed. Let’s break down the differences and the compiler’s perspective.

Memory Layout: The Crucial Distinction

The compiler’s warning stems from a fundamental mismatch in memory organization.

  • Array of Arrays (e.g., int matrix[M][N]): This represents a contiguous block of memory. Imagine a matrix as a single, long sequence of elements laid out row by row. For an M x N matrix, the memory would look like this:
